summary: The Fed path hardened again: the October minutes show 'almost all participants' expect further hikes and a couple would consider more than 25bp, with Waller keeping 50bp on the table. The Gulf flared: the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island and Iran targeted bases in Kuwait and Bahrain (intercepted), yet oil fell to 3-month lows on a US crude build. Nvidia beat and guided higher but fell; chip-export licensing and a reported Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen Thursday are the AI-policy swing factors.

risks.title: Fed hiking path and Fed leadership (Chair Warsh)
risks.status: Held 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 (Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike). Nov 18 minutes: 'almost all participants' judged further hikes would likely be appropriate; 'a couple' said more than 25bp could warrant consideration if inflation data are unfavorable; staff see inflation risks skewed up; almost all discussed AI-return and opaque AI-debt risks. Waller (CNBC, Nov 18) kept a 50bp December hike on the table (accounts of the wording differ). Earlier: October CPI core +0.3% (third straight), PPI +0.3%, retail ex-autos +0.6%, import prices +1.1%; Musalem sees 'several' hikes by spring 2027. Next: claims and Philly Fed Nov 19, Jefferson Nov 19 09:25, Cook Nov 20 12:15; November CPI lands after the Dec 9 decision
risks.odds: Dec 9 hike 100%, implied 4.175% (+30bp) (fed funds futures, Nov 18); Kalshi 25bp 91% / larger 8% (via Capp Notes, Nov 18); FedWatch 69% for 50bp of hikes by end-January (via Yahoo Finance, Nov 18)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 18 close: 13-week 4.145% (3-month high), 2Y 4.80%, 10Y 5.066% (-3.7bp), 30Y 5.412%; DXY 103.79 (3-month high); gold 3,730.6 (lowest since Sep 2025)
risks.impact: A hot claims or inflation print that revives 50bp pricing pushes the 10Y back toward 5.3% and hits long-duration tech, small caps and housing; a 25bp-and-gradual message with soft data would ease yields and help rate-sensitive groups

risks.title: US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz closure
risks.status: Nov 17-18: the US struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island 'in self-defense' (Iran says no serious damage); Iran's drones targeted Patriot systems at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain, all intercepted (Kuwait called it 'a dangerous escalation'); an ADNOC ship was struck in Hormuz (1 missing, 11 injured); a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile near Khasab, Oman (crew safe); the US and Israel are reportedly debating renewed larger action after pre-election talks collapsed; USS George Washington left for the Indo-Pacific, leaving two carriers. Earlier: Trump 'we don't need a deal with Iran' (Nov 12), IRGC mine claims, Qatar mediation continuing, Iraq resumed Kirkuk-Ceyhan exports
risks.odds: US-Iran ceasefire holds to Dec 31: 25% (Polymarket via ScanX, early Nov); no fresh reading found
risks.market_pricing: Nov 18: WTI 82.01 (-4.65%) and Brent 88.68 (-4.8%) at 3-month lows despite the attacks, after a 3.4M-barrel US crude build; OVX 49.9 (Nov 17)
risks.impact: A hit that gets through (a base, a Gulf export terminal) or renewed large-scale strikes would send Brent back above $100 and add to inflation and hike pricing; a signed deal reopening Hormuz would push Brent toward the high $70s and help consumers, transports and rate-sensitive stocks while hurting energy and defense

risks.title: AI / chip policy: Nvidia leadership, export controls and AI-debt worries
risks.status: Nov 17-18: Nvidia's first report under interim CEO Kress beat (revenue $115.8B vs $109.1B, Q4 guide $130B ±3% vs $125.1B) and excluded China data-center revenue from the outlook; the board said Huang will not return as CEO; the stock fell ~2.9% Nov 18 (fifth straight loss) and delayed its 10-Q; CoreWeave -4.1%. The FOMC minutes flagged rapidly growing, opaque AI-related debt. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 (above $70-78), trading on Nasdaq Thursday. Earlier: Huang resigned Nov 12; Commerce now requires licenses for advanced AI-chip purchases by data-center operators in several countries and closed the remote-rental loophole; Nvidia's general counsel testifies privately to House committees Dec 2
risks.market_pricing: Nov 18: SOXX 141.85 (+0.28%) after a +1.6% gap faded; QQQ 659.51 (+0.39%); SMH -10.8pp vs SPY over 1 month, -14.3pp over 3 months
risks.impact: A weak Anthropic debut, wider export rules or AI-credit stress would extend the de-rating; a strong debut and no new rules would let the beat-and-raise lift semis off the 136 higher low

risks.title: China-Taiwan tensions, chip export controls and the Trump-Xi meeting
risks.status: A Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen is reported for Thursday Nov 19, possibly with Putin, with the Iran war on the agenda (per Capp Notes; not confirmed by a primary source); SCMP reported both sides extended suspensions of some trade restrictions ahead of it. The new US AI-chip licensing rule hit Asian chip stocks Nov 17 (Taiex -2.3%, Kospi -2.6%); Kospi rebounded above 5,100 after Nvidia's results. Taiwan curbed short selling Nov 9; a report says US tariffs on Chinese chips are delayed to June 2027 (unconfirmed)
risks.market_pricing: SMH -18.3% over 3 months; SOXX 35% below its 52-week high
risks.impact: A trade thaw or eased chip rules at the meeting would help a semis rebound; new curbs, Chinese retaliation or Taiwan drills would hit semis first

risks.title: US government funding / shutdown risk
risks.status: The stopgap funds the government through Dec 11; the House has passed 3 of 12 FY2027 bills while Senate appropriations are deadlocked; the fight moves to a lame-duck session before the new Democratic Congress; no deal reported as of Nov 18
risks.impact: A December lapse would delay economic data the Fed needs and dent Q4 growth; a full-year deal or a clean CR into the new Congress removes it

risks.title: CMS anti-fraud rule for managed care (Medicare Advantage)
risks.status: New Nov 18: CMS proposed an anti-fraud rule (CRUSH); UnitedHealth fell about 6-10% (the biggest Dow drag), Humana -6%, CVS -3%, Cigna -2%; health care was the second-worst sector (-2.2%)
risks.market_pricing: XLV -2.2% Nov 18 but still +9.5pp vs SPY over 3 months
risks.impact: A broad final rule would cut managed-care margins and weigh on the Dow and health-care leadership; a narrowed rule or a long comment period would let the group recover

risks.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping
risks.status: A Houthi attack reportedly damaged Aramco offices in Riyadh (reported Nov 9, not confirmed elsewhere); Saudi Arabia warned its Yanbu Red Sea oil hub could be targeted (Nov 6); no new incident found Nov 13-18. Trump tied the US-Saudi nuclear deal to Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords (Nov 18)
risks.market_pricing: No visible Red Sea premium; Brent at a 3-month low
risks.impact: A hit on Saudi export infrastructure (Yanbu) would be a major oil shock; calm keeps the focus on Iran

risks.title: OPEC+ output policy
risks.status: Nov 1: OPEC+ kept output targets unchanged through December; next meeting Nov 29; Goldman's December Brent forecast is $105 (2027 average $88); the IEA sees a Q4 surplus
risks.market_pricing: Brent 88.68, far below Goldman's $105 December forecast
risks.impact: With Brent at 3-month lows, a cut or extended restraint on Nov 29 would put a floor under oil; a surprise increase would extend the slide and hurt energy stocks

risks.title: Israel government formation after the Oct 27 election
risks.status: Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot the mandate on Nov 8; he has 28 days (extendable by 14) and is open to including Netanyahu; Netanyahu stays caretaker PM. CENTCOM's chief met Israel's military chief in Tel Aviv Nov 18 amid talk of renewed action on Iran
risks.impact: An Eisenkot-led or unity government would likely be more cautious on Iran (mildly bearish oil and defense); a failed mandate extends caretaker uncertainty

risks.title: Russia-Ukraine war and peace talks
risks.status: US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11) focused on security guarantees, no outcome reported; Putin is reportedly expected at a Shenzhen meeting with Trump and Xi Nov 19 (unconfirmed)
risks.odds: Peace talks by Dec 31 90%, ceasefire by Dec 31 9.5%, by Mar 31 2027 23.5% (Polymarket via Rio Times, early Nov)
risks.impact: Real progress would be mildly bearish for defense and European gas; a collapse keeps the defense theme supported

risks.title: US midterm elections: divided government
risks.status: Resolved Nov 3-4: Democrats won the House and Senate; the new Congress sits in January
risks.odds: Resolved (pre-vote: Democrats Senate 73%, prediction markets via Yahoo Finance Nov 3)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 4: Dow ~+2%, S&P +1.1%; homebuilders +6.4%, defense lower
risks.impact: Gridlock limits new fiscal policy; oversight of tariffs, defense, AI and the Iran war rises
